hook.line: It's closing time at the café. Vale calls from the kitchen, and Tomás has to choose between two answers that sound almost the same but say opposite things. Two little letters decide whether you are on your way over or on your way out.
hook.es: Ya voy, Vale. Todavía no me voy.
hook.en: I'm coming, Vale. I'm not leaving yet.

examples.es: Me voy de casa de Vale.
Hernando va al parque a las cinco.
examples.en: Hernando goes to the park at five.

examples.es: Hernando se va a las cinco.

examples.en: Are you leaving already? (to a friend)

rule:
Both mean *go*, but they look in opposite directions.

*Ir* looks ahead, at where you are heading: *Voy a casa de Vale*. It wants a place, and you are travelling towards it.
*Irse* looks back, at where you are leaving: *Me voy de casa de Vale*. The place you leave is behind you, and it can drop out altogether: *Me voy*.

When someone calls you, English says *I'm coming*. Spanish says *ya voy*, because you are going towards them.

The *se* word follows the person: *me voy, te vas, se va, nos vamos*.

The same idea shows up in other pairs: *dormir* and *dormirse*, *quedar* and *quedarse*.
smallPrint: Teachers say *irse* stresses the departure and *ir* the destination: both describe the same movement, seen from opposite ends.

readAndPick.es: Me voy de casa de Vale.
Hernando se va a las cinco.

options: He went there without saying anything.

yourTurn.prompt: Choose the right form and type the whole sentence (I'm going to Vale's place): ___ a casa de Vale. (Voy / Me voy)
yourTurn.why: You are heading towards a place, so plain *ir*.

yourTurn.prompt: Choose the right form and type the whole sentence (I'm leaving here): ___ de aquí. (Voy / Me voy)
yourTurn.why: *De aquí* is the place you leave, so it needs *irse*.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish (someone calls you from the kitchen): I'm coming!
yourTurn.why: You are going towards them, so *ir*, with no *me*.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: I'm leaving now.
Type in Spanish: Hernando leaves at five.
yourTurn.answer: Hernando se va a las cinco.

yourTurn.prompt: Ask a friend if they are leaving already.
yourTurn.why: *Te* is your friend, and leaving needs *irse*.

yourTurn.prompt: Make it about *we*: Me voy mañana.
yourTurn.why: Both *me* and the verb change for *we*: *nos vamos*.

pitfalls.why: Plain *ir* wants a place to go to; leaving a place needs *irse*.
The *se* word has to match the person, so *we* is *nos*.

pitfalls.wrong: Ya me voy, Vale. (answering her call)
pitfalls.why: To say you are on your way to her, use plain *ir*; *me voy* would tell her you are leaving.

personal: Say when you are leaving home today, or where you are going next. Use *me voy* or *voy a*.
